en: The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on Trees Growing in a Garden,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperially Appointed Grand Officer of the Court of State Ceremonial and Acting Minister of the Court of State Reception,
Dharma-Transmitting Master, Subject Shi Hu, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, together with a community of bhikṣus.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the bhikṣus, saying:

“You should know this: among the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, there is a great tree named Nandana. Its spreading roots extend for five yojanas, its height is one hundred yojanas, and its branches and leaves cover fifty yojanas.”
When that host of devas goes at the proper time beneath those trees to stroll and observe, the trees immediately produce half-nūpura flowers.
Upon seeing this, the devas give rise to joy, delight, and happiness.
Not long after that, Śilāprabhasa was born again; the assembly of devaputras went there to visit and observe at the proper time, their joy and happiness increasing all the more.
Furthermore, before long, jeweled nets arise to cover its top as an adornment.
When those hosts of devas go beneath that tree at the proper time to stroll and observe, their joy and happiness increase even further.
Furthermore, not long after they were born, those hosts of devas went at the proper time to that tree to stroll and observe; having seen this, their joy and happiness increased all the more.
Furthermore, before long, the Jāmbūnada-maṇi-ghaṭṭita (Golden-Jambū-Tree-Struck) deities arrived at that tree to stroll and observe; their sense of delight and happiness increased even further.
Furthermore, before long, Kakāśya was born. The host of devas, strolling and observing at their appointed times, experienced ever-increasing delight.

Moreover, before long, trees grew in that garden and blossomed with flowers; those flowers were pure, with extraordinary and exquisite fragrances. When stirred by a gentle breeze, their scent wafted for fifty yojanas; when carried by a strong wind, it filled a hundred yojanas; and there was also a wondrous radiance that illuminated eighty yojanas.

Once those trees have blossomed, the hosts of devas, seeing the trees in full bloom, experience a joy many times greater than before; for the four months of summer, they dwell beneath the trees, enjoying themselves in delight and pleasure.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
"You should know that the trees growing in that garden possess such qualities as exquisite flowers and extraordinary fragrances that are cherished by people;
so too it is with the śrāvakas."
When that tree first produced half a *nūpura-śākhā*, it was like a śrāvaka who, having first conceived faith, leaves the household life to head toward the Path.
Furthermore, when that tree produced a *śīrṇa-patra-śākhā*, it was like a śrāvaka who has shaved off beard and hair, donned the saffron robes, and assumed the appearance of a śrāvaka.

Furthermore, when that tree produced jeweled nets, it was like a śrāvaka who, weary of all desires and abandoning unwholesome dharmas, remains far removed from various thoughts and discriminations, attaining the concentration of the joy and bliss born of seclusion, which is the First Dhyāna.

"Furthermore, when that tree produces the *cāṣaka* fruit, it is just as a śrāvaka whose external appearance is well-composed and whose inner mind dwells in tranquility; free from all discursive thought, with a concentrated mind fixed on a single object, he attains the second dhyāna, the concentration of joy and bliss born of concentration."

"Furthermore, when that tree grows into a *kūṭa-mālaka*, it is just as a *śrāvaka* who, being detached from all craving and delight, attains physical pliancy, ease, and sublime bliss, thereby achieving the third dhyāna—the concentration of sublime bliss free from joy."

"Furthermore, when that tree grew as Kakṣa, it was just like a śrāvaka who, having eliminated all sorrow, suffering, joy, and pleasure, dwells in a mind of equanimity and attains the fourth dhyāna, the concentration of pure equanimity and mindfulness."

"Furthermore, when those trees bloom with exquisite flowers and their extraordinary fragrance pervades everywhere, being cherished and delighted in by people, it is then just like a śrāvaka whose outflows (*āsrava*) have been exhausted and in whom no further outflows increase; having realized the fruit of no-more-learning (*aśaikṣa-phala*), they will not undergo further existence. Honored and revered by humans and devas, they receive great offerings—such is the correspondence between the blooming of those flowers and this matter."
The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:

"You should know that the hosts of devaputras of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, each with distinct physical forms and adorned with various exquisite ornaments, gathered and surrounded one another in the Sudharmā Hall to listen as Śakra, Lord of Devas, proclaimed the sublime Dharma."

"O Bhikṣus! Each of you has attained the realization of the fruits, being pure and perfect; you are endowed with the holy life and honored by all. Surrounded by the World-Honored One, you listen to and receive the sublime Dharma, just as those hosts of devas do."
At that time, when the bhikṣus heard the Buddha’s exposition on the tree born in the garden, each of them felt joy and exultation in their hearts, and they accepted and practiced it with faith.
*The Sūtra on the Tree Born in the Garden* Spoken by the Buddha.
